extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines for Area Chairs overseeing paper review, discussion, and decision-making for AISTATS 2026, including reviewer assignment, monitoring, meta-reviews, ethics, and procedural requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identify desk-rejection cases
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify desk-rejection cases (e.g., papers with unacceptable formatting issues, dual submissions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See FAQ for examples; check submissions quickly for desk-reject or conflict-of-interest cases and mark/forward format violations to Program Chairs if unsure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain OpenReview registration and profile
rubrics_metrics.description: Make sure your profile on OpenReview is up-to-date, including conflicts of interest and expertise topics; import all papers to your OpenReview profile; read and agree to abide by the AISTATS code of conduct.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep conflicts and expertise current so assignment/matching works correctly; agreeing to code of conduct is mandatory.

rubrics_metrics.name: Help reviewer assignments (recruit and adjust reviewers)
rubrics_metrics.description: Help reviewer assignments by recruiting expert reviewers and adjusting reviewer assignments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be flexible with papers outside your expertise and contact the Senior AC if needed; secure expert reviewers early to reduce borderline/misjudged cases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ensure each submission has four suitable reviewers
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure each submission in your batch has four suitable reviewers with diverse perspectives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Monitor assignments and make adjustments; recruit emergency reviewers if necessary, especially a week before review release.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ensure submissions have high-quality reviewers
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure the submissions have high-quality reviewers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select reviewers with appropriate expertise, and intervene (e.g., request rewrites or recruit experts) when review quality is poor or evidence for claims is missing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Monitor the review process and reviewer responsiveness
rubrics_metrics.description: Monitor the review process and ensure reviewers are responsive.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Send reminders for review submissions; check and solicit emergency reviews in the emergency review window; follow up on late or missing reviews.

rubrics_metrics.name: Request review rewrites when appropriate
rubrics_metrics.description: Request review rewrites if appropriate, ensuring evidence for claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only ask for rewrites when there is concrete evidence a review is deficient; document reasons and seek improved, evidence-based reviews.

rubrics_metrics.name: Organize reviewer discussions after author feedback
rubrics_metrics.description: Organize reviewer discussions after author feedback.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lead reviewer–AC discussions, summarize pros/cons and major disagreements, and follow up on confidential messages from reviewers/authors appropriately.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ensure engagement during author–reviewer discussion
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure engagement between reviewers and authors during the author–reviewer discussion period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encourage reviewers to acknowledge author comments, note any score changes, and ensure substantive points from authors are addressed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Make acceptance/rejection recommendations and decisions
rubrics_metrics.description: Make acceptance/rejection recommendations based on reviews, author feedback, discussions, and your own understanding of the submission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submit meta-reviews and decisions on time; base decisions on the paper, reviews, author feedback, and discussions, and justify choices clearly. Reach out early to SAC if uncertain.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide constructive feedback for rejections
rubrics_metrics.description: When recommending rejection, provide constructive feedback for authors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain the reasons for rejection clearly and helpfully so authors can understand and act on the feedback.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recommend accepted submissions for oral talks
rubrics_metrics.description: Recommend accepted submissions for oral talks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify papers that merit oral presentation and include justification in recommendations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resolve issues during the review process
rubrics_metrics.description: Resolve any issues during the review process (e.g., by recruiting emergency reviewers, addressing concerns from both reviewers and authors, and/or raising concerns with Senior ACs and Program Chairs).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be proactive in fixing problems and escalate to SAC/Program Chairs when needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Follow confidentiality requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Keep review process details confidential. Do not use submission content until publicly released.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid sharing ideas, code, or results without approval; consult SAC or Program Chairs before discussing assigned submissions with others.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adhere to best practices and professionalism
rubrics_metrics.description: Respect deadlines and respond promptly; be professional, thorough, and fair; show empathy toward reviewers facing challenges.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notify SAC if unavailable for critical periods and report unethical or suspicious behavior to SAC and Program Chairs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Writing the meta-review — focus on review content over scores
rubrics_metrics.description: When writing meta-reviews, focus on review content rather than relying solely on scores.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judge review quality rather than confidence scores alone; compare keywords from reviewers, authors, and system matches; note whether author feedback addressed reviewer concerns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Writing the meta-review — disclose external information
rubrics_metrics.description: Disclose if new, non-review information influenced your decision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If any outside information (not present in reviews) influenced your decision, explicitly state it in the meta-review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Writing the meta-review — justify overruling reviewers
rubrics_metrics.description: Justify in detail when overruling unanimous reviewer opinions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When your decision differs from unanimous reviewer recommendations, provide a clear, detailed rationale for overruling.

rubrics_metrics.name: Writing the meta-review — take a stand on borderline papers
rubrics_metrics.description: Take a stand on borderline papers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make a clear recommendation rather than deferring; provide reasoning for your position to resolve borderline cases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Writing the meta-review — counter topical bias
rubrics_metrics.description: Counter biases against less fashionable research topics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be conscious of and actively counteract biases that disadvantage work on less popular or fashionable topics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compare keywords and expertise signals
rubrics_metrics.description: Compare keywords from reviewers, authors, and system matches as part of your assessment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use keyword agreement/mismatch as an evidence point when judging reviewer suitability and review alignment with the paper.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of Generative AI in reviews and meta-reviews
rubrics_metrics.description: Large language models (LLMs) cannot be used to write reviews or meta-reviews.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refer to the Ethical Conduct for Peer Review in the Reviewer Guidelines for the policy statement. Authors may utilize LLMs for grammar checking, but they remain responsible for all content and LLMs cannot be authors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Page limits and format violations enforcement
rubrics_metrics.description: Enforce page limit and identify other format violations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Page limit is 8 pages for the main submission plus references. Other format violations include breaking anonymity, dual submission, or unauthorized format changes—mark violations and forward to Program Chairs if unsure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reproducibility checklist handling
rubrics_metrics.description: Check for the reproducibility checklist where applicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The reproducibility checklist is not a desk-reject criterion but should be checked during author feedback and remind accepted authors to include it in camera-ready versions.
